classification.difficultyReason: Requires a four-stage angle argument combining a straight angle, equal base angles, square properties and triangle angle sums.

content.prompt: The diagram shows a triangle in a square. Find the size of $\angle BQP$. Provide full reasoning.

spec.description: Unshaded square ABCD with P on AB, Q on BC and R on DC. Triangle PQR has matching single ticks on PR and RQ. The two given angles at R have their original arcs and labels.
spec.mathematics: ABCD is a square; PR=RQ; angle DRP=80 degrees; angle QRC=45 degrees. Coordinates are derived from these relationships and display no additional numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible. All derived angles remain in answer content.

answer.short: $\angle BQP=72.5^{\circ}$. Straight-line angles give $\angle PRQ=55^{\circ}$; equal base angles give $\angle RQP=62.5^{\circ}$; $\angle CQR=45^{\circ}$, so $\angle BQP=180^{\circ}-62.5^{\circ}-45^{\circ}$.
